Main holds the flicker species of Inger et al. 2014 (22 taxa) and Chatterjee et al. 2020 (9 taxa), and Agee 1971 for Heliothis zea, searched by genus name, and none is a Polygrammate species. (2014) are not in hand. acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg wait on the wanted list for the eye survey of 224 Lepidoptera species by Chan et al. (Research Square 2024), whose species table main has not read, as the desk held the Lepidoptera acuity cells of harvest-43 and harvest-46 on the same work; the acuity pair ("Polygrammate visual acuity", "Hebrew moth visual acuity") returned human acuity pages, patents, compound-eye studies of the diurnal moth Histia flabellicornis and the leafhopper Empoasca onukii, hawkmoth sensitivity and acuity work (Konstanz, SICB, Georgia Tech) and a Leps-L post on moth attraction to light, and no Polygrammate eye study.

screened.10.5962/p.266711: a 1988 note on a dominant wing-pattern mutant of Parnassius apollo in the upper Durance basin; "frequency" is the frequency of the mutant in the population (1 to 2% in the late 1970s), and no eye or photoreceptor is measured
screened.10.1093/beheco/arw168: a field test of striped, moth-like paper targets pinned to bark and shown to wild birds and to human observers; "frequency" is the spatial frequency of the stripes, and no butterfly photoreceptor is measured

note: WebSearch returned result titles and links only (no snippets), so web results were judged by title, and nothing was opened. The queue files Parnassius under "Parnasiinae" (main's methods rows for P. glacialis carry that name), a misspelling of the subfamily Parnassiinae of the swallowtail family Papilionidae (my knowledge; the GBIF API refused this machine), so the family review searched "Parnasiinae vision review" and returned only van der Kooi et al. 2021, and the queue counts the swallowtail Papilio xuthus as an order-level relative. The queue's one species is the Apollo (Parnassius apollo). The harvest's genus queries returned two studies of the eyes of the glacial Apollo, P. glacialis (Journal of Experimental Biology 2010, on four opsins and the dorsal and ventral regions of the eye; Proc R Soc B 2012, on its tiered rhabdoms), a 2012 conference abstract on the same eye, van der Kooi et al. 2021, a 2025 review of cell types in the lepidopteran compound eye, a study of olfaction and vision in host-plant location by P. apollo larvae, and genetics, conservation, taxonomy and camouflage papers; none reports a flicker fusion frequency or a photoreceptor corner frequency. Main holds the pigment peaks of P. glacialis (van der Kooi et al. 2021) and its filter pigments and eye type (Lu and Kronforst 2026), and no temporal value for any Parnassius species. "Parnassius flicker fusion" returned human flicker-fusion pages (the Wikipedia article, arXiv models of foveated graphics and of subjective time, a PMC study of peripheral flicker fusion, patents and a bioRxiv preprint on individual variation in human thresholds). "Apollo butterfly flicker fusion" returned the Wikipedia article, the NCBS, IAS and Research Matters pages of Chatterjee et al. 2020, BioStor reference 106491 and its archive.org PDF (Nakagawa and Eguchi 1994 on Papilio xuthus, which main logs as insect#392 from that address) and a Biodiversity Heritage Library part (71310) shown without a title; no title names a Parnassius photoreceptor recording. Main holds the flicker species of Inger et al. 2014 (22 taxa) and Chatterjee et al. 2020 (9 taxa), searched by genus name, and none is a Parnassius species. Haarlem et al. 2026 (flicker fusion over 237 species; its dataset is Table B.1 of a 2025 Trinity College Dublin thesis) is in the canon file and unread, so this record stays half-searched until it is logged (desk-screen.md point 8); the books by Warrant and Nilsson (2006) and Cronin et al. (2014) are not in hand. acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg wait on the wanted list: the two P. glacialis eye studies may give facet dimensions or interommatidial angles for a congener, and the eye survey of 224 Lepidoptera species by Chan et al. (Research Square 2024), whose species table main has not read, may include a Parnassius species.
